robustness.⭐ DEGENERATE_INPUT — THE BEST IN THE REP: updateWater returns a DISCRIMINATED UNION, not void: `{drew:'volume', id} | {drew:'nothing', id, reason}` (:73-75). Three named refusals, each carrying both numbers: :111 'has N boundary vertex/vertices — a surface needs at least MIN_LOOP_VERTS'; :125 'carries no absolute elevations (surface=X, bottom=Y) — refusing to guess a water level'; :138 'has non-positive depth (D m: surface X is not above bottom Y) — an empty pool is the ABSENCE of water, not water with no depth'. The header at :70 states the contract: 'the subscriber logs the reason, so an invisible pool says why'. THIS IS THE C84/RAC REFUSAL STANDARD, MET.
robustness.⭐ DISPOSAL — EXPLICIT AND REASONED: :98-101 'disposed first, so a create followed by ten updates leaves ONE group in the scene and ten disposed geometries — not eleven overlapping translucent [surfaces]'. removeWater disposes (:257), clearProjectGeometry disposes every group (:279), and :276 warns that calling dispose() in the project sweep 'leaves the next project with a dead builder' — the terminal/sweep distinction, named.
